problem: Existing language-conditioned goal navigation benchmarks focus on object-category goals, or on VLM-generated instance descriptions (GOAT-Bench, PSL) that are often wrong or ambiguous. Manual inspection of GOAT-Bench found 39.8% of instance instructions contain semantic errors (9.9%) or ambiguities (29.9%). Region-, room-level and multi-granularity goals are unexplored for lack of quality annotations.
motivation: Real users give context-dependent goals such as 'the phone on the bed with a Bluey blanket', which need fine-grained semantic and spatial disambiguation, not just object detection. Current VLMs miss distinctive cues and reason poorly about space, so auto-generated descriptions are not discriminative. A rigorous benchmark needs human-verified, discriminative descriptions at several granularities.
key_idea: Define a four-level (scene/room/region/instance) open-vocabulary language goal navigation task and build LangMap, a benchmark on HM3D with human-verified contrastive region and instance annotations in concise and detailed forms.
insight: Contrastive human annotation gives much more discriminative descriptions with far fewer words: 79.7% vs 55.9% one-to-many text-to-view matching accuracy for GOAT-Bench, using 5.2 vs 21.1 words. Ablations show that detailed descriptions raise SR (e.g. Uni-NaVid instance 26.2 to 28.8), long-tail, small and distant goals sharply lower SR, and multi-goal sequence completion is near zero (SeqSR at most 1.5), so current agents are unreliable even when per-goal SR is reasonable. Frozen-VLM 3D-Mem has the smallest head/long-tail gap, and MTU3D's explicit object memory helps multi-goal tasks.
method: Task definition: an agent starting at a random pose receives RGB, depth and odometry, and must STOP within 1 m of any object matching a natural-language goal within 500 steps. Goals are at scene, room, region or instance level, single- or multi-goal. Actions are MOVE_FORWARD 0.25 m, TURN 30°, LOOK_UP/DOWN 30°, STOP, with a Stretch-robot embodiment.

Contrastive region annotation: a panorama is captured at each region's pseudo-center. Annotators label 12 room categories and, comparing all same-category regions in a scene, write concise and detailed discriminative descriptions (926 in total). GPT-4 outputs serve as optional references, and a second round cross-checks.

Contrastive instance annotation: categories are clustered with SentenceBERT into a hierarchy of base and fine-grained categories. Annotators see all instances of a base category with views and region context and write concise (5.3 words) and detailed (15.9 words) descriptions covering attributes, spatial context and open-world semantics. All are cross-checked (7510 descriptions, 414 categories).

Task generation: scene-level tasks iterate over all categories, with a start pose 5–30 m from the nearest goal on the same floor. Room and region tasks intersect HM3D-Sem region-object mappings with the human labels. Instance tasks use the descriptions directly. This gives about 15k single-goal tasks. Multi-goal episodes chain 5 non-overlapping tasks (720 episodes, 3.6k tasks). Geodesic distance distributions are aligned across levels.
Metrics: SR and SPL for single goals. SeqSR@n counts episodes with at least n of 5 sequential goals completed. SeqSR is full completion and SeqSR-4 is at least 4.
Annotation quality evaluation: one-to-many text-to-view matching with Qwen3-VL-235B on overlapping instances, reporting accuracy and exclusive wins against GOAT-Bench.

setting.backbone: Benchmark paper. Evaluated: PSL (CLIP + trained policy), SenseAct-NN Monolithic, 3D-Mem (frozen Qwen2.5-VL-3B/7B), Uni-NaVid, MTU3D
setting.training_data: No training by the paper (evaluation only). Baselines are pretrained: Uni-NaVid on 3.6M navigation samples, MTU3D on 1M RGB-D trajectories, 3D-Mem training-free.
setting.observation: egocentric RGB + depth + odometry (Uni-NaVid uses RGB only)
setting.action_space: low-level: MOVE_FORWARD 0.25 m, TURN_LEFT/RIGHT 30°, LOOK_UP/DOWN 30°, STOP

numbers_note: Benchmark paper with no proposed navigation method. Table 3 reports baselines only, which must not be included. Only the annotation-quality numbers are the paper's own, and they do not fit the SR/SPL schema.
results: LangMap has 18,479 tasks, 414 object categories, 926 region descriptions and 7,510 instance descriptions, and beats GOAT-Bench in discriminative accuracy (79.7% vs 55.9%, +23.8%) with 4× fewer words. The best baselines, Uni-NaVid (overall SR 30.3) and MTU3D (SR 29.7), still leave large headroom, especially on long-tail, small and distant goals, and full multi-goal completion (MTU3D SeqSR 1.5, SeqSR-4 12.4).
limitations: Covers only the 36 HM3D-Sem validation scenes, single-floor navigation and simulation only, with no real-robot evaluation.
Evaluated baselines are limited in number and are not tuned or fine-tuned on LangMap (no training split analysis).
Only static HM3D scans, with no dynamic or interactive elements.
